specification.problem: Reconstruct the logical gate algebra of the bosonic-walker universal-computation scheme: dual-rail position encoding, Rx via tunnelling, Rz via detuning, and CZ via on-site Bose-Hubbard interaction, on a tiny 2-qubit instance.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single-particle 4-mode dual-rail model of 2 qubits (qubit 0 on modes 0,1; qubit 1 on modes 2,3), reduced to the 4-dimensional logical space. One Rx(theta) on qubit 0, one Rz(phi) on qubit 1, then one CZ. Out of scope: piecewise-constant graph geometry, 2D lattice layout, full bosonic many-body dynamics, swap routing, Steane code, 3D extension, ultracold-atom implementation, error correction, and the full proof of universality.

symbols.meaning: bosonic creation/annihilation operators on site i

equations.label: Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard Bose-Hubbard model as the underlying dynamics. The interaction normalization n(n-1)/2 is taken from the method sketch.
equations.justification: The abstract names the Bose-Hubbard model but gives no explicit form. This is the textbook form. The predicted U n(n-1) factor and the predicted coupling formulas J=4πa^3/m, U=2πa^3/λ are not adopted.
assumptions: The exact graph and lattice geometry are not specified

equations.label: Dual-rail encoding
equations.description: Each qubit is one walker on a two-site pair, so the number of sites is 2n, linear in the number of qubits.
equations.justification: The abstract says information is encoded in walker positions and that the vertex count is linear in the qubit number. The specific two-site encoding is a proposed instance.
assumptions: Basis index is 2*q0+q1 with qubit 0 most significant

equations.label: X rotation via hopping
equations.latex: R_x(\theta)=e^{-i\theta X/2}=\exp\!\left[i Jt\,(a_{0}^\dagger a_{1}+a_{1}^\dagger a_{0})\right],\quad Jt=\theta/2
equations.description: In the single-particle sector, hopping between the two rails of a qubit acts as the Pauli X generator, which gives an Rx rotation.
equations.abstract_quote: Arbitrary X and Z rotations are constructed
equations.justification: The abstract claims arbitrary X rotations. Hopping with sign -J gives exp(+iJtX), so Jt=θ/2 gives exp(-iθX/2) only if the sign is absorbed into the convention (apply Jt=-θ/2 for the literal -J Hamiltonian). The mechanism is the sketch's, not the paper's.
assumptions: Sign convention absorbed into the definition of t or J

equations.label: Z rotation via detuning
equations.description: A relative on-site energy offset between the two rails of a qubit, applied for time t, produces a Z rotation.
equations.abstract_quote: Arbitrary X and Z rotations are constructed
equations.justification: The abstract claims Z rotations. A detuning of magnitude Δ with Δt=φ gives this unitary up to a global phase. The mechanism is the sketch's.
assumptions: Detuning is applied locally to one site pair

equations.label: CZ via interaction phase
equations.description: The interaction phase acts only when both walkers are in the |1> rail, giving a controlled-phase gate at Ut=π.
equations.justification: The abstract states a cphase gate exists. The mechanism of bringing the walkers together is a sketch assumption. In the 4-dimensional logical space it is compiled directly as a diagonal gate.

equations.label: Target logical unitary
equations.description: Composite logical unitary for the 2-qubit instance, acting on the 4-dimensional logical register.
equations.justification: A tiny instance chosen to test the gate algebra.
assumptions: Qubit 0 is the left tensor factor

specification.initial_state: Logical |00>, i.e. one walker on site 0 and one on site 2. Other inputs are a user-chosen superposition of the four logical basis states, prepared externally.

steps.description: Apply Rx(theta) on qubit 0 as a 2x2 block on its logical subspace (hopping for Jt=theta/2).
Apply Rz(phi) on qubit 1 as a diagonal detuning phase.
Apply the CZ phase (-1 on logical |11>) from the on-site interaction at Ut=pi.

specification.measurement: Position measurement of each walker in the computational basis: a rail index of 0 or 1 gives the logical bit. A single-qubit measurement is a local measurement on one site pair. The circuit itself is measurement-free.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Decode the logical probabilities over |q0 q1> from walker positions. Basis index is 2*q0+q1.
assumptions: Reduced to the 4-dimensional logical subspace, not simulating the full bosonic Fock space
Explicit classical parameters theta and phi are compiled into gates
Swap is not included; it could be built from three CNOTs, each a CZ plus Hadamards from Rx and Rz
This verifies logical gate algebra only, not black-box query complexity
missing_information: Piecewise-constant graph geometry and the actual construction on it
Paper's actual gate schedules and how the walkers are routed
Swap gate construction on the graph
Steane code encoding and the 3D extension
Physical parameters for the optical-lattice implementation
